title: Lefties, righties and mixed-handers: The psychology of brain asymmetry, with Sebastian Ocklenburg, PhD

sentences.en: We live in a world designed for right-handed people.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个为右撇子设计的世界里。

sentences.en: If you're a lefty, you know the pain of trying to track down left-handed scissors or a pen that won't smudge as you write.
sentences.zh: 如果你是左撇子，你一定体会过寻找左撇子专用剪刀，或者寻找一支写字时不会弄脏手掌的笔有多痛苦。

sentences.en: Yet despite being overlooked by the designers of school desks, corkscrews, and can openers, lefties make up a small but consistent part of the population.
sentences.zh: 尽管学校课桌、开瓶器和开罐器的设计师们常常忽略了左撇子，但左撇子在人口中仍占有一小部分，且比例相当稳定。

sentences.en: Today we're going to talk to a psychologist who studies handedness and other aspects of brain lateralization,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将采访一位研究惯用手以及大脑偏侧化其他方面的心理学家，

sentences.en: about handedness, where it comes from, and what it can tell us about how the brain is organized.
sentences.zh: 探讨惯用手、它的成因，以及它能告诉我们关于大脑组织方式的信息。

sentences.en: So why does handedness exist in the first place?
sentences.zh: 那么，惯用手究竟为何存在？

sentences.en: Why is it more common to be right-handed than left-handed?
sentences.zh: 为什么右撇子比左撇子更常见？

sentences.en: How and when does handedness develop?
sentences.zh: 惯用手是如何以及何时形成的？

sentences.en: Is it genetically determined due to early life experiences or maybe a combination of the two?
sentences.zh: 它是受基因决定，源于早期生活经历，还是两者共同作用的结果？

sentences.en: Is there any truth to the stereotype that lefties are more creative than other people?
sentences.zh: 关于“左撇子比其他人更有创造力”的刻板印象有道理吗？

sentences.en: Are neurodivergent people more likely to be left-handed?
sentences.zh: 神经多样性群体更容易成为左撇子吗？

sentences.en: Does handedness or pawedness exist in other animals?
sentences.zh: 其他动物也存在惯用手或惯用爪的现象吗？

sentences.en: And why are left-handed people often underrepresented in brain research?
sentences.zh: 为什么左撇子在脑科学研究中往往代表性不足？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Sebastian Acklenberg, a professor of research methods and psychology at MSH Medical School in Hamburg, Germany.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是德国汉堡MSH医学院的研究方法与心理学教授塞巴斯蒂安·阿克伦伯格博士。
zh_words: 塞巴斯蒂安·阿克伦伯格

sentences.en: His research focuses on hemispheric asymmetries in the brain's language and motor systems, including handedness.
sentences.zh: 他的研究重点是大脑语言和运动系统中的半球不对称性，包括惯用手问题。

sentences.en: He has looked at how asymmetries develop, including genetic and epigenetic factors, and the neurophysiology of brain asymmetries in the prevalence of handedness in humans
sentences.zh: 他研究了这些不对称性是如何发展的，包括遗传和表观遗传因素，以及人类惯用手流行程度中大脑不对称性的神经生理学，

sentences.en: and limb preferences in other animals.
sentences.zh: 以及其他动物的肢体偏好。

sentences.en: Dr. Acklenberg is the author of many peer-reviewed journal articles, as well as the book, The Lateralized Brain,
sentences.zh: 阿克伦伯格博士撰写了许多同行评审期刊文章，以及《偏侧化的大脑》一书，

sentences.en: The Neuroscience and Evolution of Hemispheric Asymmetries.
sentences.zh: 全名为《半球不对称性的神经科学与进化》。

sentences.en: He also writes a blog for Psychology Today called The Asymmetric Brain,
sentences.zh: 他还为《今日心理学》撰写了一个名为《不对称的大脑》的博客，

sentences.en: The Psychology and Neuroscience of Left and Right.
sentences.zh: 全名为《左与右的心理学与神经科学》。

sentences.en: Dr. Acklenberg, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 阿克伦伯格博士，感谢您今天参加节目。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: I'm very happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Well, let's start by talking about how common is left-handedness.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们先从左撇子的普遍程度谈起。

sentences.en: What percentage of the population is left-handed?
sentences.zh: 左撇子占人口的百分之几？

sentences.en: So the largest meta-analyses worldwide showed that the best estimate is 10.6% of left-handed people.
sentences.zh: 全球最大规模的荟萃分析显示，最佳估算值是10.6%的人是左撇子。

sentences.en: That varies a little bit depending on location.
sentences.zh: 这个数字会根据地理位置略有波动。

sentences.en: So there are some countries where the number is a little bit lower.
sentences.zh: 有些国家的比例会稍微低一点。

sentences.en: There are some countries where it goes a little bit higher, up to like 18, 19%.
sentences.zh: 也有一些国家比例会高一些，达到18%或19%左右。

sentences.en: But there is no country in the world where there are more than 20% left-handers.
sentences.zh: 但世界上没有任何国家的左撇子比例超过20%。

sentences.en: So they're always a minority.
sentences.zh: 所以他们始终是少数群体。

sentences.en: Why might some countries have higher percentages?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些国家的比例会更高？

sentences.en: What's in play?
sentences.zh: 这其中有什么影响因素？

sentences.en: I think this has something to do with mostly cultural factors.
sentences.zh: 我认为这主要与文化因素有关。

sentences.en: So you may remember that a couple decades ago in the US, there was something called handedness retraining.
sentences.zh: 你可能记得几十年前在美国，有一种所谓的“惯用手矫正”。

sentences.en: So in schools, left-handed kids were encouraged to use the right hand for writing.
sentences.zh: 当时在学校里，左撇子孩子被鼓励用右手写字。

sentences.en: We don't do this anymore in most countries.
sentences.zh: 现在大多数国家已经不再这样做了。

sentences.en: But there are still some countries where there are sort of negative stereotypes against left-handed people.
sentences.zh: 但仍有一些国家对左撇子存在某种负面刻板印象。

sentences.en: And those countries typically have somewhat lower numbers of left-handers because, for example, teachers encourage left-handed kids to write with the right hand.
sentences.zh: 这些国家的左撇子人数通常较低，因为例如老师会鼓励左撇子孩子改用右手写字。

sentences.en: While countries that never had this relearning, for example, some Scandinavian countries, they tend to have like a little bit higher rates because in those countries,
sentences.zh: 而那些从未进行过这种矫正的国家，例如一些斯堪的纳维亚国家，其比例往往会稍微高一点，因为在这些国家，

sentences.en: also in the older generation, there are more people that are classified as left-handed in objective tests.
sentences.zh: 即使在老一辈中，通过客观测试被归类为左撇子的人也更多。

sentences.en: And that raises the question of what determines handedness.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了一个问题：是什么决定了惯用手？

sentences.en: Is it genetic?
sentences.zh: 是基因吗？

sentences.en: Is it related to prenatal or early life experiences?
sentences.zh: 是与产前或早期生活经历有关吗？

sentences.en: Or is it something else?
sentences.zh: 还是其他因素？

sentences.en: We know today handedness is a quite complicated thing.
sentences.zh: 我们今天知道，惯用手是一个相当复杂的问题。

sentences.en: So back in the day, people thought there is a handedness gene and that determines handedness.
sentences.zh: 过去人们认为存在一个“惯用手基因”，它决定了惯用手。

sentences.en: And we know genetic factors for certain play a role.
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道，遗传因素确实起了一定作用。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you look at parents and their handedness, it predicts the handedness of children.
sentences.zh: 例如，观察父母的惯用手，可以预测孩子的惯用手。

sentences.en: So two left-handed parents have a higher chance of having a left-handed child compared to two right-handed parents.
sentences.zh: 与两个右撇子父母相比，两个左撇子父母生出左撇子孩子的几率更高。

sentences.en: But like molecular genetic techniques showed that the actual amount of handedness that can be explained by these genetic factors is around a quarter.
sentences.zh: 但分子遗传学技术表明，能由这些遗传因素解释的惯用手比例实际上只有四分之一左右。

sentences.en: So 25% of handedness basically is genetic.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，25%的惯用手基本上是遗传的。

sentences.en: And we know it is not one gene.
sentences.zh: 而且我们知道这并非由单一基因决定。

sentences.en: It's about 48 different genes that play a role according to large peer-reviewed studies.
sentences.zh: 根据大型同行评审研究，大约有48个不同的基因在起作用。

sentences.en: So it's a very multifaceted phenotype.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常多维的表型。

sentences.en: And those genes have, interestingly enough, nothing to do with the hands.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这些基因与手本身毫无关系。

sentences.en: They're mostly relevant for brain development.
sentences.zh: 它们主要与大脑发育有关。

sentences.en: And that's also something people notice, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是人们注意到的一个现象，对吧？

sentences.en: So if you just look at the hands of a left-hander or a right-hander, you cannot tell whether the person is left- or right-handed.
sentences.zh: 如果你只看左撇子或右撇子的手，你是无法判断这个人是左撇子还是右撇子的。

sentences.en: That is because handedness is not caused by the hands.
sentences.zh: 这是因为惯用手并非由手造成。

sentences.en: It's caused by the brain.
sentences.zh: 它是由大脑造成的。

sentences.en: It's specifically caused by the motor cortex of the brain.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是由大脑的运动皮层造成的。

sentences.en: So the area that controls the movements.
sentences.zh: 也就是控制运动的区域。

sentences.en: And we know that the right motor cortex is controlling the left half of the body and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 我们知道右侧运动皮层控制身体左侧，反之亦然。

sentences.en: And handedness in principle represents something what we would call a hemispheric dominance.
sentences.zh: 原则上，惯用手代表了我们所说的“半球优势”。

sentences.en: It's a hemispheric dominance for fine motor behavior.
sentences.zh: 这是精细运动行为的半球优势。

sentences.en: Things like writing, things like wood carving, drawing.
sentences.zh: 比如写字、木雕、绘画等事情。

sentences.en: So everything that's complicated to do with the hands, it's more complicated than throwing a baseball or things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以所有用手完成的复杂动作，都比投掷棒球之类的动作要复杂得多。

sentences.en: And people have a dominance for that.
sentences.zh: 人们对此有一种优势偏好。

sentences.en: So left-handers, for these people, the right motor cortex is dominant for fine motor behavior.
sentences.zh: 对于左撇子来说，右侧运动皮层在精细运动行为上占主导地位。

sentences.en: And for right-handers, the left.
sentences.zh: 而对于右撇子，则是左侧占主导。

sentences.en: So this is the one part.
sentences.zh: 所以这是其中一部分。

sentences.en: So genes relevant for brain development are relevant for handedness.
sentences.zh: 因此，与大脑发育相关的基因与惯用手有关。

sentences.en: In addition to that, there are also other factors, like environmental factors, that seem to play a role for handedness.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，还有其他因素，比如环境因素，似乎也对惯用手起作用。

sentences.en: One thing that's quite interesting is that large-scale studies could show that men are more often left-handed than women,
sentences.zh: 一个非常有趣的发现是，大规模研究表明男性比女性更容易成为左撇子，

sentences.en: which suggests there is a role of sex hormones like testosterone.
sentences.zh: 这表明睾酮等性激素可能发挥了作用。

sentences.en: And there are also a couple of prenatal factors that have been associated with left-handers, for example, being breastfed plays a role,
sentences.zh: 还有一些产前因素也与左撇子有关，例如母乳喂养起了一定作用，

sentences.en: being in the twin birth plays a role, and several other factors.
sentences.zh: 双胞胎出生也起了一定作用，以及其他几个因素。

sentences.en: And also here, hormonal effects are discussed.
sentences.zh: 在这里，激素的影响也常被讨论。

sentences.en: How early in life does handedness emerge?
sentences.zh: 惯用手在生命早期何时出现？

sentences.en: I mean, can you tell whether a little baby is going to be right-handed or left-handed?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你能判断一个小婴儿将来是右撇子还是左撇子吗？

sentences.en: I can with a pretty high chance.
sentences.zh: 我可以，而且准确率相当高。

sentences.en: So it does not emerge at exactly the same time point for everyone.
sentences.zh: 它并不是在每个人身上都在同一时间点显现。

sentences.en: But it's quite fascinating research on that question.
sentences.zh: 但关于这个问题的研究非常迷人。

sentences.en: So people use very high-tech ultrasound recordings to look at unborn babies in a mother's womb and look at which thumb they like to suck or which arm they like to interact with.
sentences.zh: 人们利用高科技超声波记录来观察母亲子宫内的胎儿，观察他们喜欢吸吮哪只手的大拇指，或者喜欢用哪只手臂进行互动。

sentences.en: And there you can see, even before birth, humans have a strong preference for one side.
sentences.zh: 在那里你可以看到，甚至在出生前，人类就对某一侧有强烈的偏好。

sentences.en: And if you then just wait a couple of years and then test these babies after they've been born and after they went to primary school, and you test them at like around age six or so
sentences.zh: 如果你等上几年，在这些婴儿出生并进入小学后测试他们，比如在六岁左右时，

sentences.en: when they start to learn riding, you can predict the preferred hand for riding with a more than 96% chance from the hand that is preferred in the ultrasound
sentences.zh: 当他们开始学习写字时，你可以根据超声波中表现出的偏好手，以超过96%的准确率预测他们写字时的惯用手，

sentences.en: for like thumb sucking or movement.
sentences.zh: 无论是吸吮拇指还是动作偏好。

sentences.en: So we can tell from that research that for a large amount of people, handedness is already pretty much determined at birth or even before.
sentences.zh: 所以从这项研究中我们可以得出结论，对于大多数人来说，惯用手在出生时甚至出生前就已经基本确定了。

sentences.en: Why is it more common for people to be right-handed than left-handed?
sentences.zh: 为什么右撇子比左撇子更常见？

sentences.en: Do we even know?
sentences.zh: 我们知道原因吗？

sentences.en: That is a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: And we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: There is no published psychological research that ever answered this question.
sentences.zh: 目前还没有任何已发表的心理学研究能回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Why it is a specific to right side that's more common than the left in humans conclusively.
sentences.zh: 为什么人类偏好右侧的情况比左侧更常见，目前尚无定论。

sentences.en: There is a couple of ideas.
sentences.zh: 有一些观点。

sentences.en: And what's quite interesting is when we, for example, look at animals, we did large meter studies on partners in cats and dogs,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当我们观察动物时，比如我们对猫和狗的爪偏好进行了大规模的荟萃分析，

sentences.en: you typically find that left-handedness or left partners in that case, it's much more common than in humans.
sentences.zh: 你通常会发现，左撇子或在这种情况下“左爪”的比例，比人类要常见得多。

sentences.en: So while animals also show handedness, this very screwed distribution with the 10.6 left-handers and 89.4% right-handers in humans seems to be pretty unique.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然动物也表现出惯用手，但人类这种10.6%左撇子和89.4%右撇子的极端分布似乎是非常独特的。

sentences.en: And there have been several psychological theories why it could be the case that we have this very high preponderance of right-handedness.
sentences.zh: 关于为什么人类会有如此高的右撇子比例，有几种心理学理论。

sentences.en: And one idea why that is, is that obviously human beings learn very complicated motor behaviors from other people, right?
sentences.zh: 其中一个观点是，显然人类是从其他人那里学习非常复杂的运动行为的，对吧？

sentences.en: So example, a dad might explain his kid how to tie their shoes.
sentences.zh: 例如，父亲可能会教孩子如何系鞋带。

sentences.en: That's, of course, easier if the dad uses the same hand for explaining than the kid uses for tying the shoe themselves.
sentences.zh: 如果父亲使用的手与孩子系鞋带时使用的手相同，解释起来当然更容易。

sentences.en: The same goes for any sort of work-related thing, any sort of like production with manual activities.
sentences.zh: 任何与工作相关的事情，任何涉及手工活动的生产活动也是如此。

sentences.en: So there seems to be a benefit from having the same handedness as other people because it makes this motor learning easier,
sentences.zh: 因此，拥有与他人相同的惯用手似乎是有益的，因为它使这种运动学习变得更容易，

sentences.en: which is one of the ideas why there are so many right-handers.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么右撇子如此之多的原因之一。

sentences.en: I'm just wondering, though, it would seem to me that ambidexterity would be something that evolution would have favored, and yet it doesn't seem to be common.
sentences.zh: 不过我很好奇，在我看来，左右开弓（双撇子）应该是进化所青睐的特质，但它似乎并不常见。

sentences.en: Why aren't more people ambidextrous?
sentences.zh: 为什么不是更多人是双撇子？

sentences.en: So I think in general, in order to answer that question, we have to think a little bit about why do humans have these brain asymmetries in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我认为总的来说，为了回答这个问题，我们必须思考一下为什么人类首先会拥有这些大脑不对称性。

sentences.en: Humans are asymmetrically represented in the brain.
sentences.zh: 人类在大脑中的功能表现是不对称的。

sentences.en: Most common example would, of course, be language.
sentences.zh: 最常见的例子当然是语言。

sentences.en: So the language networks are in the vast majority of people in the left hemisphere of the brain.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数人的语言网络位于大脑左半球。

sentences.en: And most of the time, we will not notice this, but we notice this very much if we, for example, have a family member that suffers a stroke, right?
sentences.zh: 大多数时候我们不会注意到这一点，但如果我们有家人中风，我们就会非常明显地感受到，对吧？

sentences.en: Somebody has a stroke in the left hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 有人左半球中风了。

sentences.en: They often have severe language issues and then can't talk anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们往往会有严重的语言障碍，无法再说话。

sentences.en: And that doesn't happen after a stroke in the right hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 而右半球中风后并不会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: Now, you may argue, wouldn't it be better if both hemispheres would be able to control language?
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会争辩说，如果两个半球都能控制语言，不是更好吗？

sentences.en: The problem with that is a lot of the things we're doing on an everyday basis as humans are quite complicated, and they lead a lot of neural tissue to be performed.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，我们作为人类日常所做的许多事情都相当复杂，需要大量的神经组织来执行。

sentences.en: So if we had the language represented equally in both sides of the brain, we would likely need larger brains.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果语言在大脑两侧平均分布，我们可能需要更大的大脑。

sentences.en: And that, of course, would have a lot of disadvantages.
sentences.zh: 而这当然会有很多缺点。

sentences.en: For example, when it comes to births, so you would be needed to be born even earlier as they are now, and so on and so on.
sentences.zh: 例如，在出生时，你需要比现在更早出生，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So there seems to be an evolutionary force towards making brains efficient.
sentences.zh: 因此，似乎存在一种使大脑高效的进化力量。

sentences.en: So it's a division of labor that makes optimal use of the neurons we have in our head.
sentences.zh: 这是一种分工，能最优化地利用我们大脑中的神经元。

sentences.en: I think this is the main reason why so many things are asymmetrically organized and why it's not generally common that people have language on two sides
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么这么多功能是不对称组织的，也是为什么人们通常不会在两侧都有语言功能，

sentences.en: or are equally dexterous with both hands because the ambidexterity, like true ambidexterity measured with scientifically accurate methods is something that is extremely rare.
sentences.zh: 或者双手同样灵巧的原因，因为真正的双撇子，用科学准确的方法测量，是非常罕见的。

sentences.en: So in head and this research, we do distinguish a little bit between what we call mixed-handed and what we call ambidextrous.
sentences.zh: 在惯用手研究中，我们确实区分了“混合用手”和“双撇子”。

sentences.en: So a lot of people would use the right hand for pretty much everything they do.
sentences.zh: 很多人几乎所有事情都用右手。

sentences.en: And some people use the left hand for pretty much everything they do.
sentences.zh: 有些人几乎所有事情都用左手。

sentences.en: And there are some that are in between, right?
sentences.zh: 还有一些人介于两者之间，对吧？

sentences.en: So you may know some people that, for example, write with the left and they draw with the left, but then they throw a baseball with the right
sentences.zh: 你可能认识一些人，比如他们用左手写字和画画，但投掷棒球时用右手，

sentences.en: and use a broom with the right and so on.
sentences.zh: 用扫帚时用右手，等等。

sentences.en: These people, however, they're not ambidextrous.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些人并不是双撇子。

sentences.en: They're mixed-handed, right?
sentences.zh: 他们是混合用手，对吧？

sentences.en: They can do certain activities better with the left hand and certain activities better with the right hand.
sentences.zh: 他们能用左手更好地完成某些活动，用右手更好地完成另一些活动。

sentences.en: For someone who qualifies truly ambidextrous, that person would be equally as accurate and equally as fast with both the left hand and the right hand.
sentences.zh: 对于真正符合双撇子定义的人来说，他们用左手和右手应该同样准确、同样快速。

sentences.en: And this is, for example, for writing, extremely rare.
sentences.zh: 而这在写字方面，是非常罕见的。

sentences.en: There's not a lot of really big studies on ambidexterity, but we would estimate it's about 0.1% of the population.
sentences.zh: 关于双撇子的研究并不多，但我们估计它约占人口的0.1%。

sentences.en: So roughly 1 in 1,000 people.
sentences.zh: 也就是大约每1000人中只有1人。

sentences.en: And it often has a lot to do with people training this actively, right?
sentences.zh: 这通常与人们的主动训练有很大关系，对吧？

sentences.en: So there are some people who want to be ambidextrous.
sentences.zh: 有些人确实想成为双撇子。

sentences.en: For example, it's something like tennis players sometimes do.
sentences.zh: 例如，网球运动员有时会这样做。

sentences.en: They actively train the non-dominant hand to be more surprising in the game and so on and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们主动训练非惯用手，以便在比赛中更具出其不意的效果，等等。

sentences.en: But what we often find is that a lot of people who think they're ambidextrous, if you actually test them and you do like a couple of standard psychological hand skill
sentences.zh: 但我们经常发现，许多自认为是双撇子的人，如果你真的测试他们，并进行一些标准的心理学手部技能

sentences.en: and hand preference tasks, they do not turn out to be ambidextrous.
sentences.zh: 和手部偏好任务，结果发现他们并不是双撇子。

sentences.en: They turn out to be mixed-handed.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是混合用手。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在休息一下。

sentences.en: When we return, I'll talk with Dr. Acklenberg about whether lateralization is also common in animals and how to tell if your pet is left or right pawed.
sentences.zh: 节目回来后，我将与 Acklenberg 博士探讨侧向性在动物中是否也很常见，以及如何判断你的宠物是左撇子还是右撇子。

sentences.en: And we talked a moment ago about handedness or pawedness in animals.
sentences.zh: 我们刚才谈到了动物的惯用手或惯用爪现象。

sentences.en: Are they only mammals that exhibit this?
sentences.zh: 只有哺乳动物表现出这种特征吗？

sentences.en: And what does asymmetry look like across the animal kingdom?
sentences.zh: 动物界中的不对称性又是怎样的呢？

sentences.en: Yes, so people thought back in the day that handedness is something that's only been shown by humans and they could not have been more wrong.
sentences.zh: 是的，过去人们认为惯用手只是人类才有的特征，但这种想法大错特错。

sentences.en: So in general, we could show in a large-scale study where we compared findings from studies looking at partners and other forms of limb preferences in animals
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我们在一项大规模研究中对比了关于动物肢体偏好等方面的研究发现，

sentences.en: that it is the rule, not the exception, that animals show some sort of preference.
sentences.zh: 结果显示，动物表现出某种偏好才是常态，而非例外。

sentences.en: Whether that be partners in cats or dogs or flipperedness in turtles,
sentences.zh: 无论是猫狗的惯用爪，还是海龟的惯用鳍，

sentences.en: there is a wide variety of these asymmetries.
sentences.zh: 这些不对称现象多种多样。

sentences.en: And it can show, obviously, on a behavior level, but it can also show in other things.
sentences.zh: 显然，这不仅体现在行为层面，还体现在其他方面。

sentences.en: For example, the most primitive organism that has been shown to show symmetries is actually a worm that doesn't even have limbs, say elegans.
sentences.zh: 例如，目前已知表现出对称性（不对称性）的最原始生物，其实是一种连肢体都没有的蠕虫，比如秀丽隐杆线虫。

sentences.en: And here it could be shown that neurons that were relevant for olfaction, so the worm-smelling different chemical substances, were asymmetrically organized.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，与嗅觉相关的神经元，即蠕虫感知不同化学物质的神经元，其组织结构也是不对称的。

sentences.en: So we know in general that this seems to be a really core evolutionary principle of brain or nervous system organization.
sentences.zh: 所以我们普遍认为，这似乎是大脑或神经系统组织中一个非常核心的进化原则。

sentences.en: What's a little bit interesting in regard to humans is what I already said, that humans seem to be a little bit unique in the way that our asymmetries are very strong,
sentences.zh: 关于人类，有一点比较有趣，正如我刚才所说，人类在不对称性表现得非常强烈这一点上似乎有些独特，

sentences.en: that we have a very strong handedness, very strong preference for the right hand,
sentences.zh: 我们有非常明显的惯用手，对右手有极强的偏好，

sentences.en: but also that we have a very pronounced language asymmetry and we have many other forms of asymmetries.
sentences.zh: 而且我们的语言不对称性也非常显著，同时还存在许多其他形式的不对称性。

sentences.en: That may be the case because we're doing quite complicated things with language and water behavior that other animals do not do in that sense.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为我们在语言和行为上处理着相当复杂的事情，而其他动物在这一层面上并不这样做。

sentences.en: So it's a lot of neural tissue we need for that, so there is a strong pressure to make this as efficient as possible, so we have strong asymmetries.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们需要大量的神经组织来支持这些功能，所以为了尽可能提高效率，我们进化出了强烈的不对称性。

sentences.en: But in general, you will find the symmetries in pretty much all animals people have looked at.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，你在几乎所有被研究过的动物身上都能发现这种不对称性。

sentences.en: And it's quite interesting.
sentences.zh: 这非常有趣。

sentences.en: You can also, if you're interested as a listener of the podcast, if you want to look into that in your pet, you could, for example, do something like a food-reaching task.
sentences.zh: 如果你作为播客听众对此感兴趣，想观察一下你的宠物，你可以尝试做一些简单的测试，比如食物抓取任务。

sentences.en: So if you have some sort of like paper roll and you put a little bit of cat food or dog food into that, and then you can look at which paw the animal would use to get the food out.
sentences.zh: 你可以准备一个纸卷，在里面放一点猫粮或狗粮，然后观察动物会用哪只爪子把食物掏出来。

sentences.en: And then you can do that maybe like five or six times.
sentences.zh: 你可以重复测试五六次。

sentences.en: And if you notice your animal is always using the same paw, you can be pretty sure your cat is left paw to right paw.
sentences.zh: 如果你发现你的宠物总是用同一只爪子，那么你基本可以确定你的猫是左撇子还是右撇子了。

sentences.en: And obviously, animals also have a lot of other preferences.
sentences.zh: 当然，动物还有许多其他的偏好。

sentences.en: So for example, you can look at things like the sleeping side.
sentences.zh: 例如，你可以观察它们的睡眠侧向偏好。

sentences.en: So if the cat curls up to the left or curls up to the right side, if you put them into their like little basket and you're sleeping,
sentences.zh: 比如猫在睡觉时是向左蜷缩还是向右蜷缩，当它们躺在小篮子里睡觉时，

sentences.en: and many other things.
sentences.zh: 还有许多其他方面。

sentences.en: So it is something that's not only affecting our lives as humans a lot, but also those of our pets and many other animals.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不仅深刻影响着我们人类的生活，也影响着我们的宠物和许多其他动物。

sentences.en: Now, do the brains of people who are left-handed and right-handed look different?
sentences.zh: 那么，左撇子和右撇子的大脑看起来有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: Are they different structurally?
sentences.zh: 它们的结构有区别吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they're different structurally in terms of the brain areas that are directly relevant to handedness.
sentences.zh: 是的，在与惯用手直接相关的脑区方面，它们的结构确实不同。

sentences.en: So they are their motor cord, he says.
sentences.zh: 也就是运动皮层。

sentences.en: They're not differently structured in a lot of other different brain areas.
sentences.zh: 但在其他许多脑区，它们的结构并没有差异。

sentences.en: So these ideas that maybe left-handers have, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 所以那些认为左撇子可能，我不知道，

sentences.en: higher or lower intelligence, that's not the case.
sentences.zh: 智商更高或更低的想法，是不成立的。

sentences.en: So it is something that affects the motor system.
sentences.zh: 这只是一种影响运动系统的特征。

sentences.en: It's something that is reflected in the structure of the motor system, but it doesn't go beyond that.
sentences.zh: 它反映在运动系统的结构中，但仅限于此。

sentences.en: And I think that the brain areas that are directly relevant to a function, like the motor cortex that is allowing me to write, they show changes.
sentences.zh: 我认为与特定功能直接相关的脑区，比如让我能够书写的运动皮层，确实会表现出变化。

sentences.en: Many other brain areas typically don't.
sentences.zh: 而其他许多脑区通常不会。

sentences.en: Now, a lot of people might not be aware, but we also favor other body parts.
sentences.zh: 很多人可能没意识到，我们对身体其他部位也有偏好。

sentences.en: So we're not just left-handed or right-handed, but we might be left-footed or right-footed.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅有惯用手，还有惯用脚。

sentences.en: But if you're left-handed, are you more likely to be left-footed or left-eyed?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你是左撇子，你是否更有可能是左脚或左眼占主导？

sentences.en: Yes, so there is a fascinating number of these behavioral asymmetries.
sentences.zh: 是的，这些行为不对称现象的数量非常惊人。

sentences.en: And there's always like something people haven't thought of, and then there's a new research paper, and I'm like, oh, that's really cool.
sentences.zh: 总会有一些人们没想到的新发现，每当看到新的研究论文，我都会觉得，哦，这太酷了。

sentences.en: So yes, people have a favorite foot.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们确实有惯用脚。

sentences.en: And yes, headedness and footedness are related.
sentences.zh: 而且惯用手和惯用脚确实是相关的。

sentences.en: They're not 100% related.
sentences.zh: 但它们并非百分之百相关。

sentences.en: So we had a large study on that showing that around 65% of right-handers are also right-footed.
sentences.zh: 我们的一项大型研究显示，大约 65% 的右撇子也是右脚占主导。

sentences.en: There are also these sensory biases.
sentences.zh: 此外还有感官偏好。

sentences.en: So people have a favorite ear to listen to a door, or like a favorite eye to look to a microscope.
sentences.zh: 比如人们有接听电话时习惯用的耳朵，或者使用显微镜时习惯用的眼睛。

sentences.en: And what I find very fascinating is also that people have side asymmetries in different forms of social touch, right?
sentences.zh: 我觉得非常迷人的一点是，人们在各种社交接触中也存在侧向不对称性，对吧？

sentences.en: So for example, if you give somebody a high-five, you have a preferred hand to give a high-five.
sentences.zh: 例如，当你和别人击掌时，你会有习惯使用的手。

sentences.en: If people kiss another person, they have a strong preference to turn their head to one side.
sentences.zh: 当人们亲吻他人时，他们有强烈偏好将头转向某一侧。

sentences.en: It's quite interesting if you kiss people to the left or the right side for all your life to try the other one.
sentences.zh: 如果你一辈子都习惯向左或向右亲吻别人，尝试换另一侧会非常有趣。

sentences.en: So most participants say that that's an extremely weird feeling.
sentences.zh: 大多数参与者都表示，那是一种极其奇怪的感觉。

sentences.en: People have a favorite side to hug other people on.
sentences.zh: 人们拥抱他人时也有习惯的侧向。

sentences.en: People have a favorite side to taste food on.
sentences.zh: 人们咀嚼食物时也有习惯的侧向。

sentences.en: So their favorite food tastes maybe a little bit different if you chew it on the left or on the right side.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在左侧或右侧咀嚼，同样的食物尝起来可能味道会略有不同。

sentences.en: And so on and so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类，不胜枚举。

sentences.en: So these asymmetries in behavior that, of course, reflect asymmetries in the brain to some extent, that are very ancient, they're like popping up left and right
sentences.zh: 这些行为上的不对称性，在某种程度上反映了大脑的不对称性，它们非常古老，在日常生活中随处可见，

sentences.en: in everyday life, even today.
sentences.zh: 即使在今天也是如此。

sentences.en: And most people don't really notice it because they don't even actively think about it.
sentences.zh: 大多数人并没有真正注意到这一点，因为他们甚至不会主动去思考。

sentences.en: But if you really monitor yourself a little bit when you're going through your day and you just actively pay attention to behaviors where you can choose
sentences.zh: 但如果你在日常生活中稍微留意一下自己，主动关注那些你可以选择左侧或右侧的行为，

sentences.en: either the left or the right side, you will notice that you have a lot of these preferences that really barely change, right?
sentences.zh: 你会发现你有很多这种几乎从不改变的偏好，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't start like suddenly hugging somebody on the left side if you always do the right side.
sentences.zh: 如果你总是习惯从右侧拥抱别人，你不会突然开始从左侧拥抱。

sentences.en: So these are very deeply ingrained behavioral preferences.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都是根深蒂固的行为偏好。

sentences.en: Now, there's a stereotype that creative, artistic people are more likely to be left-handed.
sentences.zh: 现在有一种刻板印象，认为富有创造力、艺术气息的人更有可能是左撇子。

sentences.en: Is that borne out by the research?
sentences.zh: 研究证实了这一点吗？

sentences.en: No, it is not.
sentences.zh: 不，并没有。

sentences.en: So if you look at like studies, large scale, highly controlled psychological studies from the last couple of years, it is pretty clear that if objective tests
sentences.zh: 如果你查看过去几年里大规模、高控制的心理学研究，很明显，如果使用客观的创造力测试，

sentences.en: of creativity are used, there are no significant differences between left and right-handers.
sentences.zh: 左撇子和右撇子之间并没有显著差异。

sentences.en: So there's very creative left-handers, but there's also extremely uncreative left-handers.
sentences.zh: 所以，既有非常有创造力的左撇子，也有极其缺乏创造力的左撇子。

sentences.en: And there's very uncreative right-handers, but there's also very creative right-handers.
sentences.zh: 同样，既有非常缺乏创造力的右撇子，也有非常有创造力的右撇子。

sentences.en: Where there is a large and significant effect is in people's attitudes and beliefs towards the creativity of left-handers.
sentences.zh: 真正存在巨大且显著效应的是人们对左撇子创造力的态度和信念。

sentences.en: So both left-handed people and right-handed people strongly believe that left-handed people are more creative.
sentences.zh: 左撇子和右撇子都强烈地认为左撇子更有创造力。

sentences.en: And this also affects job choices.
sentences.zh: 这也影响了职业选择。

sentences.en: So for example, parents tell their kids more often to maybe go into a creative profession when they're left-handed.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果孩子是左撇子，父母会更频繁地建议他们从事创造性职业。

sentences.en: So there seems to be some sort of like stereotype effect here based on what, for example, has been communicated in the media about left-handedness in the past decade.
sentences.zh: 所以这里似乎存在某种刻板印象效应，这基于过去十年媒体对左撇子的宣传。

sentences.en: That is, however, not backed up by modern, highly controlled psychological science.
sentences.zh: 然而，这并没有得到现代高控制心理学科学的支持。

sentences.en: Now, you've written about how left-handed athletes tend to be more successful at their sports than right-handedness.
sentences.zh: 你曾写过关于左撇子运动员在体育运动中往往比右撇子更成功的内容。

sentences.en: What's behind that?
sentences.zh: 这背后的原因是什么？

sentences.en: That's also quite interesting because it seems to be an effect of their rarity.
sentences.zh: 这也很有趣，因为这似乎是由于他们的稀缺性带来的效应。

sentences.en: So it's not like that left-handed athletes per se have some like higher ability in sports.
sentences.zh: 并不是说左撇子运动员本身在体育方面就有更高的天赋。

sentences.en: For certain types of sports, such as racket sports like tennis and like combat sports, like for example, boxing,
sentences.zh: 对于某些类型的运动，比如网球等球拍类运动，以及拳击等格斗类运动，

sentences.en: left-handers have an advantage and that advantage is surprise.
sentences.zh: 左撇子具有优势，而这种优势就是“出其不意”。

sentences.en: Like so most people, if they train, they train with right-handed people just because they're much more right-handed people.
sentences.zh: 大多数人在训练时都是和右撇子对练，仅仅因为右撇子的人数要多得多。

sentences.en: So this is what people are prepared if they go into like a boxing fight or a tennis match.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们参加拳击比赛或网球比赛时，他们对此是有准备的。

sentences.en: And then if somebody comes up when they're left-handed, they might've played against left-hander or fought against the left-hander before.
sentences.zh: 如果突然遇到一个左撇子，他们可能以前也和左撇子交过手，

sentences.en: But in general, like the probability is much lower.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，这种概率要低得多。

sentences.en: So it's unlikely they have as much training experience as when fighting or playing a right-handed opponent.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不太可能像面对右撇子对手那样拥有丰富的训练经验。

sentences.en: And that shows.
sentences.zh: 而这就会产生影响。

sentences.en: So there are data that show that left-handed people in these sports are more successful.
sentences.zh: 有数据表明，在这些运动中，左撇子确实更成功。

sentences.en: And that leads to like a certain over-representation.
sentences.zh: 这导致了某种程度上的“过度代表”。

sentences.en: So there are, for example, more left-handers and professional boxers than in the general population.
sentences.zh: 例如，职业拳击手中的左撇子比例高于普通人群。

sentences.en: But of course, the advantage would disappear at some point if there are too many left-handers because then they're as calm as right-handers.
sentences.zh: 但当然，如果左撇子太多，这种优势在某种程度上就会消失，因为那时他们就和右撇子一样常见了。

sentences.en: But it doesn't mean they're like generally better at sports.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着他们普遍更擅长体育运动。

sentences.en: It's just the system basically gives them an advantage due to their rarity.
sentences.zh: 这只是因为他们的稀缺性，系统基本上给了他们一种优势。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a minute about neurodivergent people.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈神经多样性人群。

sentences.en: Are they more likely to be left-handed than right-handed?
sentences.zh: 他们比右撇子更容易成为左撇子吗？

sentences.en: And if so, why?
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，为什么？

sentences.en: That's a quite interesting area of research because the answer is yes.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的研究领域，因为答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: So there have been large-scale meta-analyses, for example, on people in autism spectrum disorders.
sentences.zh: 例如，针对自闭症谱系障碍人群已经进行了大规模的荟萃分析。

sentences.en: And people on the spectrum typically have a higher chance of being left-handed, being mixed-handed than the general population.
sentences.zh: 谱系障碍人群成为左撇子或混合用手者的几率通常比普通人群更高。

sentences.en: And why this is more common in neurodiverse individuals, it's not well understood.
sentences.zh: 至于为什么这在神经多样性个体中更常见，目前还不是很清楚。

sentences.en: So we know there are certain genetic pathways that are overlapping between like being on the spectrum but this is just a really, really tiny amount of variance.
sentences.zh: 我们知道在谱系障碍和惯用手之间存在某些重叠的遗传途径，但这只是极小的一部分差异。

sentences.en: But the general finding is quite strong.
sentences.zh: 但总体发现是非常强有力的。

sentences.en: So the effects are quite large.
sentences.zh: 所以这种效应相当显著。

sentences.en: And we're trying to understand why in research.
sentences.zh: 我们正在研究中试图理解其中的原因。

sentences.en: What got you interested in this line of research?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你对这个研究方向感兴趣的？

sentences.en: And are you a lefty or a righty?
sentences.zh: 你是左撇子还是右撇子？

sentences.en: I'm right-handed.
sentences.zh: 我是右撇子。

sentences.en: I'm not left-handed at all.
sentences.zh: 我完全不是左撇子。

sentences.en: I'm really like 100% right-hander.
sentences.zh: 我真的是百分之百的右撇子。

sentences.en: So I'm generally really interested in how the brain generates behavior.
sentences.zh: 我通常对大脑如何产生行为非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And I find it extremely fascinating that these evolutionary, very old structural organization principles like all brains have two halves, right?
sentences.zh: 我发现这些进化上非常古老的结构组织原则极其迷人，比如所有大脑都有两个半球，对吧？

sentences.en: If you look at the human brain, it's the most striking visual thing about it, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你观察人类大脑，这是它最引人注目的视觉特征，对吧？

sentences.en: It has two halves.
sentences.zh: 它有两个半球。

sentences.en: Why does it have two halves, right?
sentences.zh: 为什么它有两个半球呢？

sentences.en: So in understanding this and understanding how this affects psychology and how this affects our everyday lives or everyday behavior
sentences.zh: 理解这一点，以及理解它如何影响心理学和我们的日常生活或日常行为，

sentences.en: is something I always found incredibly fascinating because these are like very old structural things, but they're still affecting us to the very day.
sentences.zh: 是我一直觉得非常迷人的地方，因为这些是非常古老的结构性事物，但它们至今仍在影响着我们。

sentences.en: So for example, if you look at people doing selfies for social media, there's a very strong effect that people would put their left cheek firSt.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你看人们在社交媒体上拍自拍，有一个非常明显的效应，就是人们会先露出左脸。

sentences.en: And research has shown that people also find portraits of people that show their left cheek in front more emotionally warm or emotionally positive.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，人们也觉得展示左脸的肖像画在情感上更温暖或更积极。

sentences.en: So people like naturally, without this cognitively reflecting on the psychological science behind this, go into an asymmetric posture to have other people like their pictures more.
sentences.zh: 所以人们在没有对背后的心理学科学进行认知反思的情况下，自然而然地采取了不对称的姿势，以让别人更喜欢他们的照片。

sentences.en: And that's not something where they're like, oh, I do this now.
sentences.zh: 这不是他们刻意去做的。

sentences.en: This is something that's very deeply ingrained and it's based on very old
sentences.zh: 这是根深蒂固的，并且基于非常古老的

sentences.en: neuroscientific processes.
sentences.zh: 神经科学过程。

sentences.en: I find that very fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常迷人。

sentences.en: Now, I've read that left-handed people are often underrepresented in psychological and brain research and that they're often screened out of research studies.
sentences.zh: 我读到过左撇子在心理学和脑科学研究中往往被低估，而且经常被排除在研究之外。

sentences.en: Why does that happen?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: And is that a problem?
sentences.zh: 这是一个问题吗？

sentences.en: That happens and it is a problem.
sentences.zh: 确实发生了这种情况，而且这确实是个问题。

sentences.en: So the reason why that happens is that researchers in psychology for a long time thought that left-handers may introduce noise into the data.
sentences.zh: 发生这种情况的原因是，心理学研究人员长期以来认为左撇子可能会给数据带来干扰。

sentences.en: They make it more complicated to analyze the data.
sentences.zh: 他们使得数据分析变得更加复杂。

sentences.en: Let me explain why.
sentences.zh: 让我解释一下原因。

sentences.en: So for example, if you do a study on the psychology of language and you use an MRI scanner to look at the brain activation of people during a language task.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你进行一项语言心理学研究，并使用核磁共振扫描仪观察人们在语言任务期间的大脑激活情况。

sentences.en: So if you look only at right-handed people, you would see a left-hemispheric activation during language task in about 95 to 100% of people.
sentences.zh: 如果你只观察右撇子，你会发现大约 95% 到 100% 的人在语言任务期间表现出左半球激活。

sentences.en: So almost everyone.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有人都是这样。

sentences.en: So if you now look at left-handed people, you will find this left-sided activation of the brain in only 75% of left-handers.
sentences.zh: 如果你现在观察左撇子，你会发现只有 75% 的左撇子表现出这种左侧大脑激活。

sentences.en: 25 of them would show an unusual right-hemispheric activation.
sentences.zh: 其中 25% 的人会表现出不寻常的右半球激活。

sentences.en: This is just normal diversity.
sentences.zh: 这只是正常的差异性。

sentences.en: This is how human brains are organized.
sentences.zh: 这就是人类大脑的组织方式。

sentences.en: There's nothing bad or wrong with that.
sentences.zh: 这没什么不好或不对的。

sentences.en: But if you now would do a psychological experiment, you would just do a population sampling where 10% of people are left-handed and 90% are right-handed,
sentences.zh: 但如果你现在要做一个心理学实验，进行人口抽样，其中 10% 是左撇子，90% 是右撇子，

sentences.en: you would have a few people that would show a reverse pattern of results and their brain activation, the left-handers that have the right-hemispheric activation, than the others.
sentences.zh: 你会发现有少数人的大脑激活模式与其他人相反，即那些表现出右半球激活的左撇子。

sentences.en: And if you now do a statistical analysis of data that's very much focused on the average across all participants,
sentences.zh: 如果你现在对非常关注所有参与者平均值的数据进行统计分析，

sentences.en: what you will find is then the overall effect is a little bit like less clear, it's a little bit more noisy because you have some people that are having a reverse effect.
sentences.zh: 你会发现整体效应变得不那么清晰，干扰更多，因为有些人表现出了相反的效应。

sentences.en: But as psychologists, of course, we should embrace the diversity.
sentences.zh: 但作为心理学家，我们当然应该拥抱这种多样性。

sentences.en: We should make sure in order to do good science that we include all aspects of the human brain in our study because what happens if we systematically exclude a group of people,
sentences.zh: 为了做好科学研究，我们应该确保在研究中涵盖人类大脑的所有方面，因为如果我们系统性地排除了一部分人，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: what happens maybe if, for example, there are clinical intervention planned on things like that, they might not be optimal for left-handed people.
sentences.zh: 如果计划进行临床干预，结果可能对左撇子来说不是最优的。

sentences.en: They might not be great for left-handed people.
sentences.zh: 它们对左撇子来说可能并不理想。

sentences.en: They might even be detrimental for left-handed people.
sentences.zh: 它们甚至可能对左撇子有害。

sentences.en: That's the big issue that brain stimulation techniques, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是脑刺激技术面临的一大问题，对吧？

sentences.en: So there's psychologists who use stimulation of certain brain areas as therapeutical tools.
sentences.zh: 有些心理学家利用特定脑区的刺激作为治疗手段。

sentences.en: For example, the idea in depression that that could be helpful.
sentences.zh: 例如，在抑郁症治疗中，人们认为这可能会有帮助。

sentences.en: And what happens there is that the stimulation in those studies, those clinical studies, is often on one side.
sentences.zh: 而在那些临床研究中，刺激通常只作用于大脑的一侧。

sentences.en: But what our research would suggest is that may not be optimal because if people have a switched lateralization of their emotion, that's also more common left-handers,
sentences.zh: 但我们的研究表明，这可能并非最佳方案，因为如果人们的情绪偏侧化发生了转换（这在左撇子中更为常见），

sentences.en: they might not benefit from a treatment that is good for the majority of people.
sentences.zh: 他们可能无法从对大多数人有效的治疗中获益。

sentences.en: So what needs to be done is in both basic psychological research and clinical psychological research, especially if it comes to brain stimulation of one half of the brain,
sentences.zh: 因此，无论是在基础心理学研究还是临床心理学研究中，特别是在涉及大脑半球刺激时，都需要采取相应的措施，

sentences.en: is that left-handers should be included.
sentences.zh: 那就是应该将左撇子纳入研究对象。

sentences.en: And we just need a different way of analyzing the data.
sentences.zh: 我们只是需要一种不同的数据分析方法。

sentences.en: We shouldn't just like really mush all people together.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该把所有人混为一谈。

sentences.en: but we should more look at like the individual variation and also reflect that in our statistics, right?
sentences.zh: 我们应该更多地关注个体差异，并将其反映在统计数据中，对吧？

sentences.en: So you can say like there are some people like 75% on the left and the other on the right and be like show these groups different or something like that.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，有些人75%倾向于左侧，另一些人倾向于右侧，然后将这些群体区别对待，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But we definitely should not continue to exclude left-handed people in psychology.
sentences.zh: 但我们绝对不应该在心理学研究中继续排斥左撇子。

sentences.en: And just to wrap up, what are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 最后总结一下，你现在在研究什么？

sentences.en: What are the big questions you're still trying to answer?
sentences.zh: 你还在试图回答哪些重大问题？

sentences.en: What we're working on now is we're trying to understand what happens when people are training their non-dominant hand.
sentences.zh: 我们目前正在研究人们训练非惯用手时会发生什么。

sentences.en: So we have studies where people like volunteer to like train their non-dominant hand a little bit over time and then we repeatedly look at their brains and try to find out what can
sentences.zh: 我们开展了一些研究，让志愿者随着时间推移对非惯用手进行少量训练，然后我们反复观察他们的大脑，试图找出什么

sentences.en: be learned, what cannot be learned, and what is the neuroscience behind that.
sentences.zh: 是可以习得的，什么是无法习得的，以及其背后的神经科学原理。

sentences.en: And I think other research areas that are quite interesting are topics like epigenetics, like what are the molecular processes over which these environmental factors are affecting
sentences.zh: 我认为其他一些非常有趣的研究领域还包括表观遗传学，比如环境因素通过什么样的分子过程影响

sentences.en: handedness.
sentences.zh: 惯用手。

sentences.en: There's a lot of neuroimaging actually going on, so what neurotransmitters and so on are mapping on brain scans and things like that.
sentences.zh: 目前确实有很多神经影像学研究，比如神经递质等是如何在脑部扫描中呈现的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And I think in general people try to understand much more what is actually happening on a biological level.
sentences.zh: 我认为总的来说，人们正试图更深入地了解生物学层面到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: Well, Dr.
sentences.zh: 好的，阿克伦伯格博士，

sentences.en: Acklenberg, I want to thank you for joining me.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: It's been a very interesting conversation.
sentences.zh: 这是一次非常有趣的谈话。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you,
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，

sentences.en: Kim.
sentences.zh: 金。

sentences.en: I was happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。
